clue.text: Very merry British game of chance

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for British
a lottery-style game of drawn numbers

explanation.surface: A British gambler gets jolly over a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very merry' is a polite way of saying very drunk, which is the slang sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, and 'very merry' is a jocular euphemism for that state.

clue.text: Bird left Noah's vessel

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for left
the boat Noah built for the Flood

explanation.surface: A bird flew from Noah's boat, as in the Flood story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as a verb of departing; here it is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark, such as the skylark, is a songbird, so a specific kind of bird.

clue.text: Anais, the novelist, and Arachne support opera conductor

indicators.note: in a down entry, things that support another go beneath it

blocks.note: Puccini's opera Tosca
Anaïs Nin, the diarist and novelist
the setter is Arachne, who refers to herself as I

explanation.surface: A novelist and the setter back an opera conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in the clue stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor, an example of a conductor.

clue.text: Huge flag showing Egyptian god

blocks.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
the flag is a kind of iris plant

explanation.surface: A giant banner bears a picture of an Egyptian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' suggests a banner, but it is the plant: yellow flag is a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and the underworld.

clue.text: Delay as Hettie gets changed

indicators.note: letters that get changed are put into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
a woman's name, used for its letters

explanation.surface: Someone is held up while Hettie changes her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' looks like a link but its letters are part of the fodder: AS plus HETTIE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause or hold back before acting, a verb synonym of delay.

clue.text: Adherents ask for new work by Conrad

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Followers request a fresh book by Joseph Conrad.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart of Darkness is Joseph Conrad's 1899 novella of a journey up the Congo, so one of his works.

clue.text: They buy jumpers under a shilling

indicators.note: in a down entry, a part under another is written below it

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
creatures that jump, such as grasshoppers

explanation.surface: Customers pick up sweaters for a shilling or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' suggests British sweaters, but it means things that hop. The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers are people who purchase goods, so the noun stands for 'they buy'.

clue.text: After time he receives thank you letter from Athens

indicators.note: what comes after something is placed following it
receiving something means taking it on immediately next

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for time
taken as written
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Eventually a man gets a thank-you note sent from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thank you letter' looks like one phrase, but 'letter' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a letter used in Athens.

clue.text: Mad Hatter, free from then on

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's Mad Hatter has been at liberty since then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland looks like one name, but 'Mad' is the signal for the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereafter is an adverb meaning after that time, i.e. subsequently.

clue.text: Woman is scared at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman on a boat is frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: Cressida is the faithless heroine of Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida is a female given name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Cook perhaps might need this in kitchen

blocks.note: first meaning: Alastair Cook was a batsman who opened the innings for England
second meaning: a gadget for getting into tins or bottles

explanation.walkthrough: The capital C hides the cricketer: Alastair Cook opened the batting for England at cricket. Read as lower-case, a cook in the kitchen would need a tin or bottle device.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the opening batsmen are called openers; in a kitchen, a can or bottle opener is a tool.

clue.text: Old playwright wangled a senatorship

indicators.note: to wangle is to manipulate or fiddle, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient dramatist used underhand means to obtain a seat in the senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the comic dramatist of ancient Athens, so he is an old playwright.

clue.text: "Competence" was Brown's nickname!

blocks.note: first meaning: ability to do something
second meaning: the byname of Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener

explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot Brown earned his nickname by telling clients their estates had great potential for improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Capability is the power to do something well, and it was also the famous nickname of Lancelot Brown.

clue.text: She has royal status in Pomerania

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following word, spelt out in its letters

blocks.note: the run of letters in the middle of the place name

explanation.surface: A woman holds a royal title in the Baltic region of Pomerania.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or a rajah's wife, so she is a woman of royal standing.

clue.text: It picks up and carries branch to Nick

blocks.note: a fork is a place where a road or river branches
to nick and to lift are both slang for steal

explanation.surface: Something that collects and carries a branch to a man called Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name with its capital, but it is the British slang verb for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A forklift truck raises loads on its prongs and moves them, so it literally picks up and carries.

clue.text: Student leader of insurrection gets told off and set free

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a learner driver displays an L plate
the opening letter of the word
to berate is to scold

explanation.surface: A student ringleader of a rebellion is scolded and then released.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated means freed from captivity or restriction, a past-tense synonym of set free.

clue.text: Bastard met bimbo — it's a disaster waiting to happen!

indicators.note: as an adjective bastard means corrupt or not genuine, so the letters are debased into another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cad has taken up with an airhead, and trouble is sure to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a time bomb is a situation certain to cause trouble eventually, like a bomb on a timer.

clue.text: Large building consisting of one third basalt and quartz

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is its first two letters, the opening portion kept

blocks.note: the opening third of the rock name
quartz is a crystalline form of silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A big edifice is made partly of basalt rock and quartz.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church or hall of Roman origin, so a large building.

clue.text: Created money, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of a word, not its spelling

blocks.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone apparently made cash, so the gossip goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to produce offspring, so bred means brought into being, i.e. created.

clue.text: Join former drinkers and non-drinkers inside church

indicators.note: being inside means sitting within the other group

blocks.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members have given up drink
TT stands for teetotal
standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Become a member of a church where ex-drinkers and teetotallers mix.
explanation.walkthrough: The teetotallers go inside the recovering alcoholics, and the church follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach is to fasten or connect, a verb synonym of join.

clue.text: Reckons girl's right to become a sportswoman

blocks.note: to figure is to reckon or calculate
a girl's name
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a girl has the right to turn into an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has', joining the girl to the right, which follows her.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who competes in figure skating on ice is a sportswoman of that discipline.

clue.text: Up to usual nasty tricks, insurgents lynch leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Rebels are up to their usual dirty tricks, lynching their leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Until is a preposition meaning up to a given time, as in 'open until six'.

clue.text: Clergyman to be beheaded soon

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A priest is going to be executed shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic or literary word for soon, presently, in a little while.

clue.text: German is embraced by brother in restaurant

indicators.note: to be embraced is to be held within something else's arms

blocks.note: short informal form of brother
the German word for 'is'

explanation.surface: A German man is hugged by his brother in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German is' together means the German word for is, so 'is' does double duty in the surface but belongs with German.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant, typically French in style.

clue.text: Former partner pretending to be difficult

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
acting is putting on a pretence

explanation.surface: An ex putting on an act just to be awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting task or person demands great effort or precision, so is difficult.

clue.text: Make final alteration to sweet course

indicators.note: altering the final part means the last letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: a syllabub is a creamy dessert of whipped cream and wine

explanation.surface: Put the finishing touch to a dessert course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet course' looks like a single phrase for pudding; 'sweet' is the wordplay and 'course' alone the definition. The last letter B becomes S.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of a course of study, so the two words name the same thing.

clue.text: Concealing ill-treatment

blocks.note: first meaning: keeping out of sight
second meaning: a thrashing or beating

explanation.definitionFit: Hiding is the participle of hide, keeping out of view, and also a noun for a severe beating.
